list.name: trace_id
list.label: Trace ID
list.description: Paste the X-Trace-Id header or the trace_id from a response body.

options.content:
Paste a trace id into the **Trace ID** box at the top. Both panels below fill in:

* **The trace** -- every span, across the Go gateway, the Go order and inventory services, the Redis queue, and the Node worker. Click any span and choose *Logs for this span*.
* **Its log lines** -- from every service that touched the request, in one stream, filtered by `trace_id` in Loki's structured metadata.

A trace id is on the `X-Trace-Id` response header and in the `trace_id` field of every JSON response body, including error bodies. `./scripts/chaos.sh` prints the ones it generated.

This works because every log line carries `trace_id` and `span_id` (`internal/obs/slog.go` for Go, `src/logger.ts` for Node) and because Loki keeps them as structured metadata rather than labels -- a trace id as a label would mean one Loki stream per trace.

panels.title: Trace $trace_id
panels.description: Expect gateway POST /checkout -> orders POST /orders -> inventory POST /reserve, plus orders.insert, an orders.fulfil publish span, and -- after the queue gap -- an orders.fulfil process span from the Node worker with its own POST /commit back into Go.

panels.title: Every log line in trace $trace_id
panels.description: The filter is on structured metadata, which is how the trace id survives without becoming a label.

panels.title: Recent errors across all services (click TraceID to jump)
panels.description: The reverse direction: start from a log line and open its trace. The TraceID link comes from the derivedFields in deploy/grafana/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yaml.

panels.title: Service graph
panels.description: Built by Tempo's service-graphs metrics generator from the parent/child edges in the traces. The queue edge only appears here if the trace context survived the async hop -- an orphaned worker span shows up as a disconnected node, which makes this panel a propagation smoke test.
